messages:
mike: Heads up — node gpu-gn-05 started throwing Xid 13s and ECC corrected counts spiking. I started a partial drain earlier, taking it out of rotation for critical inference lanes.

sarah: Ugh. Which GPU / serial? Any pattern (temps / power)?

mike: GPU0 shows most of the noise. nvidia-smi and dmesg snippets below. Serial on chassis sticker: SN:G7031ABCD123

```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,PCI
GPU 0:
  ECC Errors
    Volatile: 12
    Aggregate: 12
Xid 13: GPU kernel panic at seq=324
[dmesg] NVRM: Xid (13) 00000000: 79:00:02
```

Also saw brief PCI reset around 09:12 UTC, temps normal (~65C), power 200W.

josh: Opened a vendor ticket VT-90877 (3rdPartyGPU). Vendor asked for serial + `nvidia-smi -q` + PCB photos. Marked as "depot swap eligible" pending DOA confirmation.

rma-bot: RMA ticket VT-90877 created. Vendor: 3rdPartyGPU. Swap type: depot_exchange. ETA replacement: 7-10 business days. Required docs: serial, `nvidia-smi -q` output, 2 photos (front/back), PO# or asset tag.

vendor-ops: For depot swap we need the following from site ops: 1) Photo of PCB showing firmware label, 2) Close-up of connector pins, 3) Confirmation that card was removed unopened (no customer damage). Ship-from must be US-only depot on this account (account contract restricts cross-border depot swaps). Depot: SEATTLE-DEPOT-4.

lina: Noted on shipping constraints — this node is in us-west1-b. Good (no cross-region). Capacity note: we lose ~8 vGPUs for the next 7-10 business days. Recommend draining remaining similar nodes proactively to check for early failures.

priya: Can we avoid customer impact? Suggest: 1) shift 10% of inference traffic to eu-west failover, 2) enable lighter batching on us-west to reduce p99 latency when remaining GPUs pick up load. Someone from release/traffic team to approve? @lina @mike

mike: Approved. I'll patch the autoscaler policy to lower bin-packing on long jobs and kick small jobs to eu-west. Command used to drain: `kubectl drain gpu-gn-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` then `kubectl cordon gpu-gn-05`.

sarah: When you pull the card, please also run full `nvidia-bug-report.sh` and upload tarball to the VT ticket. Vendor often rejects RMAs without it. Also photograph the sticker with serial and the PCB.

josh: Added PO# 2024-RINF-3421 to VT-90877. Vendor requested we include asset tag and purchase invoice for faster turnaround. Marking ticket high priority.

vendor-ops: Reminder: depot swap SLA is contingent on DOA check. If vendor finds physical damage they convert to a parts-only RMA. Please ensure packaging and photos show no physical impact. Also note: replacements are shipped back-to-back but Customs Hold can add 2-3 days if flagged; keep us updated.

mike: Card pulled at 11:03 UTC, took photos, uploaded `nvidia-bug-report` tar to the ticket. Current host status: drained and cordoned. Spare pool: 2 hot spares in us-west that can be provisioned tonight.

lina: I'll schedule the swap window for 02:00-04:00 UTC to minimize traffic. @priya will coordinate routing change.

priya: Routing change done — willilng to run the canary for 30m after traffic shift. I'll post latency numbers.

mike: FYI vendor contact name is "R. Chen" and their case id is VND-14512 (internal). They asked for the PCB photo to be annotated with the area showing the burnt traces if any. Nothing burned here, just ECC/Xid noise. :thumbsup:

josh: After swap completes, we should re-run full soak on the replacement for 48 hours before rejoining pool. Add to post-replace checklist.

priya: Canary results: p50 unchanged, p95 up from 240ms -> 265ms during traffic move, p99 stable. No customer-facing errors yet. Monitoring on. :eyes:

mike: Closing loop here — VT-90877 updated with shipment label once vendor provides it. Will follow up when RMA is picked up. If anything else pops, ping me.

sarah: Thanks — please add the node and serial to the hardware RMA spreadsheet (RMA-Track-2024).
